title: at edit is kind-blind and the refusal's own remedy walks a non-test row into carrying both file and prose, which at lint has no rule for
body:
`at edit` is KIND-BLIND in both directions, and the route into the resulting contradictory row is the tool's OWN refusal remedy.

MEASURED by ic 2026-08-29 against the delivered pair `30a2dd81`, in a throwaway `intent init` fixture, never the live estate. Independently reproduced by vc in a separate fixture under a fake HOME, both directions.

## The route in is the tool's own advice

`at new` on a taken id refuses correctly at rc=1 -- that part works and is not the defect. Its remedy says, on a row of ANY kind:

    To re-cite it, `intent at edit ST0001 AT-01.1 --file <path>`

The remedy is kind-blind. On a `kind: non-test` row, `--file` is the wrong flag: `--prose`'s own help, and `docs/reference/intent-at.md`'s flag table in the same words, define prose as "What a non-test row asserts INSTEAD OF a file".

Following the remedy verbatim returns rc=0 (`ok: AT-01.1 re-cited`) and leaves:

    {"id":"AT-01.1","kind":"non-test","file":"some/test/path.rs","prose":"original prose","status":"n-a"}

Both fields present, on a kind whose vocabulary says they are alternatives.

## It is the verb, not the flag -- the mirror confirms it

`at edit --prose` on a `kind: test` row also returns rc=0:

    {"id":"AT-01.2","kind":"test","file":"real/test.rs","prose":"eyeballed it, no file involved","status":"green"}

So `at edit` never consults the row's kind when deciding whether a field applies. Neither direction is refused and neither is warned about.

## `at lint` has no rule for it, and this was measured with a WORKING instrument

Both rows were driven OFF `to-write` first (`at na` and `at green`), because `at lint` exempts `to-write` from L2/L3 -- so a `conform` verdict on to-write rows means EXEMPT, not CHECKED, and would have been a blind green.

With the exemption gone, `at lint ST0001` reports exactly one finding -- `AT-01.2 cites a file that does not exist` -- and rc=1. That rc=1 is the positive control: lint is not stuck-green, it fires on this very corpus, and it still says nothing about either row carrying both fields.

## Why medium rather than minor

No data is destroyed and no exit code lies. What makes it worth a row is the path: the operator most likely to produce the impossible state is the one who did what the error message told them to do. A defect you can only reach by ignoring the tool is a sharp edge; one you reach by obeying it is a trap.

## Two candidate fixes, not ruled between

1. Make the remedy kind-aware -- name `--prose` for a non-test row and `--file` for a test row. Cheapest, and closes the route that produces the state in practice.
2. Make `at edit` refuse a field that does not apply to the row's kind, and give `at lint` a rule for the both-fields state. Closes the state itself rather than one route to it.

They are not alternatives in the long run; (1) without (2) leaves the state reachable by hand.

## Related, not duplicated

`kind` is unwritable on both edit verbs by declared design (`8aebe2ce`), so an operator who reaches this state cannot correct it by changing the row's kind. That is a separate stated hole, and it is what makes the contradictory row sticky.
